prompt.context: Our client is a $500M machine manufacturing company with 5 business units in the U.S. He hired us to work with the Electronic Machines division, which is a $25M business with 5% EBITA. He envisions growing the division to a $100M business with 20% EBITA. These machines are used to manipulate steel in different industries and are about the size of a PC.
prompt.question: The client wants to know whether this growth goal is possible, or what he should do with this business unit. How would you approach this question and what would you recommend him?

clarifying_info.q: What is the size of the electronic machine industry?
clarifying_info.a: It is a $1B industry, stable (not growing, not shrinking).

clarifying_info.q: What is the client's competitive position?
clarifying_info.a: Our client is #3 out of 10 players. The 2 biggest competitors have 40-42% market share each.
All companies offer products with same quality, same service, same warranty — there is no point of differentiation.

clarifying_info.q: How are the machines sold / what is the sales channel?
clarifying_info.a: Machines are sold through distributors (regional, local — size is not relevant). Distributors only carry 2 brands each; they need to keep inventories of spare parts. Machine sales represent only 5% of distributor revenues; distributors make money by selling consumables.

clarifying_info.q: What types of machines are there?
clarifying_info.a: Two types: old technology (in the market for 40 years) and new technology (10 years). 90% of the market is old technology. Despite benefits of the new technology, customers are not willing to pay the price.

clarifying_info.q: Where does the client's revenue come from?
clarifying_info.a: The client entered the market 10 years ago by inventing the new technology. 60% of their revenues comes from new technology machine sales, 40% from old technology.

clarifying_info.q: What is the current cost structure?
clarifying_info.a: Materials: 60% of COGS. Labor: 15% of COGS. Overhead: 25% of COGS. COGS is ~80% of price (giving 5% EBITA after 15% fixed costs). For a $2,800 new technology machine: COGS = $2,240, Fixed costs = $420, EBITA = $140.

clarifying_info.q: Are there options to produce in other countries?
clarifying_info.a: Yes. China: materials 50% of current cost, labor $2/hr, overhead savings 60%, distribution $50/machine. Mexico: materials 50% of current cost, labor $4/hr, overhead savings 50%, distribution $20/machine. Malaysia: materials 30% of current cost (70% savings), labor $2/hr, overhead savings 30%, distribution $50/machine. Fixed costs remain the same ($270 after moving).

exhibits.title: Revenue Stream Overview
exhibits.shows: A table showing the breakdown of the $1B market and the client's $25M revenue by machine type (old technology vs. new technology), with market share percentages and dollar amounts for each segment.
exhibits.data: Market old technology: 90% ($900M); Market new technology: 10% ($100M); Client old technology: 40% of client revenue ($10M); Client new technology: 60% of client revenue ($15M)

exhibits.title: Cost and Pricing Math — Current vs. Proposal and Country Comparison
exhibits.shows: Two tables: (1) Current situation vs. proposal comparing price, COGS components (materials, labor, overhead), fixed costs, and EBITA for a new technology machine priced at $2,800 vs. $1,800. (2) A country comparison table showing variable cost breakdowns (materials, labor, overhead, distribution) and EBITA for US, China, Mexico, and Malaysia at a price of $1,800.
exhibits.data: Current: Price $2,800, Total COGS $2,240, Materials $1,344, Labor $336, Overhead $560, Fixed costs $420, EBITA $140 (5%). Proposal at $1,800: Total COGS $1,170, Fixed costs $270, EBITA $360 (20%). Country variable costs at $1,800: US $2,240; China $993 (materials $672, labor $45, overhead $224, distribution $50); Mexico $1,066 (materials $672, labor $90, overhead $280, distribution $20); Malaysia $892 (materials $403, labor $45, overhead $392, distribution $50). Total cost including fixed: US $2,660; China $1,263; Mexico $1,336; Malaysia $1,162. EBITA: US $140; China $537; Mexico $464; Malaysia $638.

framework: Understand the current business situation: $25M revenue, 5% EBITA, and what it would take to reach $100M and 20% EBITA
Analyze revenue growth levers: market dynamics, competitive landscape, pricing, and distribution channel constraints
Analyze cost reduction levers: current cost structure, outsourcing / offshoring options, and how much cost reduction is required
Synthesize into a recommendation with risks and next steps

questions.prompt: Understand the business: What does 5% EBITA mean in dollar terms, and what gap must be closed to reach the goal?
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate: 5% EBITA on $25M = $1.25M today. Target is 20% EBITA on $100M = $20M. The gap is large and requires both significant revenue growth (4x) and margin expansion (from 5% to 20%). Candidate should recognize this requires fundamental change, not incremental improvement.

math.setup: Current EBITA = 5% x $25M. Target EBITA = 20% x $100M.

questions.prompt: Revenue analysis: The client sells new technology at $2,800 but 90% of the market buys old technology at $1,800. What would happen if the client lowered its new technology price to $1,800?
questions.guidance: Candidate should recognize the pricing mismatch is the core obstacle to market penetration. If price drops to $1,800 (matching old technology), the client could potentially compete for the 90% of the market on old technology. However, the candidate must immediately ask: can the client maintain/improve profitability at $1,800? This bridges into the cost analysis.

math.setup: At current cost structure, if price drops from $2,800 to $1,800: COGS = $2,240, Fixed costs = $420, Total cost = $2,660. Revenue = $1,800.
steps: To reach 20% EBITA at $1,800: target cost = $1,800 x 0.80 - fixed costs
Required cost reduction = $2,660 - $1,440 = $1,220, which is ~46% reduction
math.answer: At current cost structure, selling at $1,800 yields a loss of $860/machine. To achieve 20% EBITA, total cost must fall to ~$1,440 — requiring roughly 46% cost reduction.

questions.prompt: Cost analysis: How can the client reduce costs by ~46%? Explore outsourcing options.
questions.guidance: Candidate should propose offshoring/outsourcing production. The interviewer provides data for China, Mexico, and Malaysia. Candidate should build a comparison of total costs per machine in each country and identify the best option. Malaysia is optimal.

math.setup: Compare total cost (variable + fixed) per machine at price $1,800 for each country. Variable cost = materials + labor + overhead + distribution. Fixed costs = $270 in all non-US locations.
steps: China: Materials $672 + Labor $45 + Overhead $224 + Distribution $50 = Variable $993 + Fixed $270 = Total $1,263 → EBITA = $1,800 - $1,263 = $537 (29.8%)
Mexico: Materials $672 + Labor $90 + Overhead $280 + Distribution $20 = Variable $1,066 + Fixed $270 = Total $1,336 → EBITA = $1,800 - $1,336 = $464 (25.8%)
Malaysia: Materials $403 + Labor $45 + Overhead $392 + Distribution $50 = Variable $892 + Fixed $270 = Total $1,162 → EBITA = $1,800 - $1,162 = $638 (35.4%)
math.answer: Malaysia has the lowest total cost at $1,162/machine, yielding EBITA of $638 (35.4%) — well above the 20% target. The company should move production to Malaysia.

questions.prompt: Distribution channel: How can the client grow revenues from $25M to $100M given that distributors only carry 2 brands and it must displace incumbents?
questions.guidance: Candidate should recognize the distribution bottleneck: distributors carry only 2 brands, the top 2 competitors dominate, and machine sales are only 5% of distributor revenue so there is little incentive to switch. Strong answer suggests offering regional exclusivities to motivate distributors, leveraging lower price as a demand-creation tool, and creating pull demand so customers ask for the new technology machine.

brainstorming.prompt: What risks and opportunities should the client consider when moving production to Malaysia and repositioning price?

categories.name: Operational / Quality Risks
ideas: Impact on product quality during transition
Learning curve at new production site
Cultural and management challenges operating in Malaysia
Government and regulatory requirements in Malaysia

categories.name: Competitive Risks
ideas: Competitors can lower their prices as well, neutralizing the pricing advantage
Top 2 competitors may respond by also offshoring to maintain cost position
Risk of price war eroding industry margins

categories.name: Distribution Risks
ideas: Distributors may not switch brands even at lower price
Exclusivity deals may be costly or create channel conflict

categories.name: Opportunities
ideas: Lower price could drive demand shift from old to new technology in the US
New production base in Asia enables entry into Asian markets under a different brand
Cost structure improvement makes the business more defensible long-term
If successful, model could be applied to other business units

recommendation: Move production from the U.S. to Malaysia to reduce per-unit cost from $2,660 to $1,162, enabling 20%+ EBITA at a price of $1,800
Negotiate with distributors by offering regional exclusivities to incentivize them to carry the client's new technology machines
Once operations are stable (quality, distribution), lower price to $1,800 to drive demand from old technology to new technology in the U.S.
Leverage the new Asian production base to sell machines in Asia under a different brand, creating an additional revenue stream to help reach the $100M target
risks: Competitors can lower their prices as well, eroding pricing advantage
Quality and execution risk during the production transition to Malaysia
Distributors may not respond to exclusivity offers quickly enough
Revenue ramp-up may take time; achieving 4x revenue growth to $100M is an ambitious target
next_steps: Conduct operational due diligence on Malaysia manufacturing partners and assess quality control capabilities
Model distributor exclusivity deal economics to determine feasible terms
Develop a phased transition plan for moving production with milestones for quality and output
Identify Asian market entry opportunities and assess brand strategy for the region
